Two qualifying findings; the rest already-good or rejected-with-reason.

FILED: F1 task-9e21c3f285b3d7d0 (p2)  ·  F2 task-d8970b41d745e066 (p2)
No priority-1 correctness finding — both qualifiers are efficiency.

blocks.text: F1 — chat_live transcript: unbounded @messages + O(n)/O(k^2) group_agent_rows recomputed every render

content.value: Filed: task-9e21c3f285b3d7d0 (priority 2). Confidence HIGH on the algorithmic costs (code-evident); MEDIUM on absolute wire bytes (not captured live).

Named failure mode: a long Studio agent session (the sessions epic runs multi-hundred-turn conversations, each turn appending user/assistant/tool rows) accumulates the entire transcript in @messages with NO cap. Every write is socket.assigns.messages ++ [message] (chat_live.ex:1186,1387,3465,3717); grep found zero Enum.take/slice/limit on messages.

blocks.value:
# chat_live.ex ~2184 — grouping recomputed INLINE in the template, not memoized:
<%= for item <- group_agent_rows(@messages) do %>   # O(n) over full history, each render

# group_agent_rows/1 children reduce — O(k^2) for a k-child agent brood:
Map.update(acc, pid, [m], &(&1 ++ [m]))              # list append is O(k)

content.value: Three compounding costs: (1) group_agent_rows rebuilds spawn-map + children reduce + flat_map over the FULL transcript on every render that touches @messages = O(n)/turn = O(n^2)/session; (2) the &1 ++ [m] child append is O(k^2) per agent brood; (3) per-socket heap holds the whole transcript for the socket lifetime and the transcript comprehension re-diffs all rows on each append (wire O(n)/turn). Fix menu: memoize grouped rows in an assign updated incrementally on append; window/paginate the transcript; replace ++ with prepend+reverse-once. Protective measurement (delegated to the fix task): a group_agent_rows micro-bench at N=2000 vs N=200 asserting non-superlinear, plus a bounded-retention test.

blocks.text: F2 — Authenticated Studio LiveViews run full DB projections on the discarded disconnected mount

content.value: Filed: task-d8970b41d745e066 (priority 2). Confidence MEDIUM — double-invocation + unguarded loads are static-evident; absolute ms/query savings not measured live.

For an auth-gated LiveView the disconnected mount render is discarded the instant the WS connects and mount runs again. These surfaces run the expensive projection UNGUARDED, so it executes on both mounts — the disconnected copy is pure waste (no crawler consumes an auth page).

blocks.value:
# board_live.ex — Board.snapshot OUTSIDE the connected? guard (heaviest: ~3 queries):
def mount(_p,_s,socket) do
  if connected?(socket) do                 # :197 — guards ONLY subscribe + timer
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(...); Process.send_after(self(), :refresh, ...)
  end
  socket |> assign(:board, Board.snapshot(dataset: @dataset)) ...   # :203 — runs on BOTH mounts

# Sibling unguarded loads:
#   inbox_live.ex:91        load_inbox (fetch_tickets + presenter)
#   settings_live.ex:69     assign_page -> assign_plugin_rows
#   org_admin_live.ex:32    list_organizations + per-org org_status + Audit.recent(20)
#   staleness_live.ex:52    load_books + per-book detect_stale

content.value: Already-good contrast (do NOT touch): bulldocs_live.ex:76 + sheets_reader + quiz_play load on the dead render DELIBERATELY and correctly — they are PUBLIC pages whose crawlers/unfurlers run no JS and need the OG head + body from the disconnected render (documented at bulldocs_live.ex:76-90). Honest tradeoff: guarding removes first-paint content on the disconnected render (skeleton until WS connects). Protective measurement (delegated): an Ecto SQL.Sandbox query-count test asserting connected?==false issues zero board-projection queries.

Streaming isolation: chat per-text-delta touches only @streaming (chat_live.ex:945); the transcript comprehension is not re-diffed per token, and @streaming.stable_html memoizes the stable prefix — textbook design.
gantt_data(card): board_live.ex:2887 recompute is guarded behind expanded?(@expanded, card) — bounded to the open card, not all cards.

<% x = @a %> in HEEx (~30 sites, editor.ex / components.ex / sheet_grid.ex etc.): modern HEEx tracks assigns referenced inside <% %> blocks — a style smell, not a change-tracking breaker. Rejected as tidiness.

LiveComponent choices: sheet_grid (80 handle_event), paper_field_block (3), tree_codelist_field (4) are genuinely stateful; graph_view has no handle_event but uses update/2 to scope derivation per assign change — converting to a function component would recompute on every parent render. All justified.

Per-socket desk memory: the paper block list is STREAMED (mount.ex:270 stream(:paper_blocks)); media_files/ref_candidates/revisions/graph_data initialize empty and load on demand; panes are bounded by desk size. No unbounded collection sits in the desk socket.

Module-size extract seams: chat_live (5055 lines), sheet_grid (3489), board_live (3343) are fat, and studio_live is already decomposed into a studio_live/ subtree (mount/blocks/paper_canvas/handlers/shared). But the brief admits a split ONLY where a NAMED upcoming change is made cheaper — none was identified. Splitting for line-count alone is the tree-tidiness the charter rejects.

Streaming isolation: chat per-text-delta touches only @streaming (chat_live.ex:945); the transcript comprehension is not re-diffed per token, and @streaming.stable_html memoizes the stable prefix — textbook design.

gantt_data(card): board_live.ex:2887 recompute is guarded behind expanded?(@expanded, card) — bounded to the open card, not all cards.

<% x = @a %> in HEEx (~30 sites, editor.ex / components.ex / sheet_grid.ex etc.): modern HEEx tracks assigns referenced inside <% %> blocks — a style smell, not a change-tracking breaker. Rejected as tidiness.

LiveComponent choices: sheet_grid (80 handle_event), paper_field_block (3), tree_codelist_field (4) are genuinely stateful; graph_view has no handle_event but uses update/2 to scope derivation per assign change — converting to a function component would recompute on every parent render. All justified.

Per-socket desk memory: the paper block list is STREAMED (mount.ex:270 stream(:paper_blocks)); media_files/ref_candidates/revisions/graph_data initialize empty and load on demand; panes are bounded by desk size. No unbounded collection sits in the desk socket.

Rejected with reason

Module-size extract seams: chat_live (5055 lines), sheet_grid (3489), board_live (3343) are fat, and studio_live is already decomposed into a studio_live/ subtree (mount/blocks/paper_canvas/handlers/shared). But the brief admits a split ONLY where a NAMED upcoming change is made cheaper — none was identified. Splitting for line-count alone is the tree-tidiness the charter rejects.
